about: How Kami's answers are scored after the truth check. Version 0 is a seed written by Claude from the project's rules; XIAO's critique of the analysis batch replaces it (version 1+). Rules with a `check` are scored by code (scripts/coachlm/verify.ts, src/lib/coach/rubric.ts); every rule's text goes to the judge (scripts/coachlm/judge.py). Weights are relative.

rules.text: The first one or two sentences answer the question directly (the move, the verdict, or who is ahead), before any background.
It explains why with a Go reason the student can reuse (shape, a weak group, sente and gote, territory against influence, what happens later), not just KataGo's numbers.
Claims about lines are shown, not only told: it points to at least one variation or diagram the student can hover.
When a diagram was built for the answer, the answer uses it to show the idea on its own.
No filler, flattery or talk about being an AI.

check.pattern: \b(great question|as an ai|i hope this helps|let me know if)\b

rules.text: Long enough to teach, short enough to read: about 40 to 350 words.
Plain language pitched at the student's level; Go terms are fine, engine jargon (visits, policy, PV) is not.
